description: Three stacked single-panel plots of calculated phonon (vibrational) dispersion relations — ab-initio/DFT band structures — each with "Energy (THz)" on the y-axis and high-symmetry points of the Brillouin zone along the x-axis; no scale bars, legends or numeric data labels are drawn on the curves. (a) FeAl: y-axis ticks 0,2,4,6,8,10 with the frame extending slightly above 10 THz; path Γ–M–R–Γ–X. Low-frequency branches rise from Γ = 0 to a maximum just under 8 THz near M, while the high-frequency branches sit near 10 THz at Γ, dip slightly, then reach ~11 THz near R, so the two groups are separated by an optical gap. (b) Fe3Al: y-axis ticks 0,2,4,6,8,10; path Γ–X–M–R–Γ; bands are dense and continuous from 0 to above 10 THz with no optical gap and no imaginary (negative) frequencies. (c) Fe3AlC: y-axis ticks 0,5,10,15,20,25; a sparse high-frequency group lies between ~20 and ~26 THz (one branch is flat at 20 THz from Γ to X), clearly separated from a dense group below ~15 THz. The figure shows that FeAl and Fe3AlC display a gap between light-Al-derived high-frequency and heavy-Fe-derived low-frequency branches, whereas Fe3Al bands are gapless and dynamically stable.

observations.observation: All three panels are phonon dispersion curves with 'Energy (THz)' as the y-axis quantity and high-symmetry Brillouin-zone points on the x-axis; no scale bar, no legend and no printed data values appear on the curves.

Panel (a) plots FeAl along Γ–M–R–Γ–X with y ticks 0,2,4,6,8,10; its lower band group reaches a maximum just below the 8 THz gridline while the upper group lies near the 10–11 THz region, leaving a visible optical gap between the groups.
Panel (b) plots Fe3Al along Γ–X–M–R–Γ with y ticks 0,2,4,6,8,10; the branches form a continuous manifold with no optical gap and none dip below 0 THz.

Panel (c) plots Fe3AlC with the y-axis extended to 25 THz (ticks 0,5,10,15,20,25) and shows a sparse high-frequency group between roughly 20 and 26 THz, including a branch that is flat at 20 THz from Γ to X, separated from the dense lower manifold below about 15 THz.
The caption states that the figure shows vibrational band structures for (a) FeAl, (b) Fe3Al and (c) Fe3AlC compound.

The citing text states that the vibrational band structures for FeAl, Fe3Al and Fe3AlC phases were calculated with the SGGA approximation (later it refers to the present calculation as a GGA approach).

The citing text attributes the high-frequency branches of FeAl mainly to the low-mass Al atoms and the low-frequency bands primarily to the high-mass Fe atoms, with the two bands separated by an optical gap.

The citing text states the FeAl optical gap is around 0.7 THz and that its width matches that calculated for FeAl-B2 or DO3, while Fe3Al-L12 results were close to Ni3Al-L12; this numeric value is not printed anywhere in the figure.

The citing text states that the calculated Fe3Al structure is stable in the present work although the literature reports the L12 structure is not mechanically stable within the GGA approximation, an anomaly attributed to sensitivity to the choice of functional.
The citing text states that for Fe3AlC no significant differences were noted between the present (GGA) calculations and those reported in the literature (SGGA approach).

The group is composite only in the sense of three related phonon dispersions of different compounds; all panels share the same modality (calculated dispersion curves) and none contains a micrograph, spectrum or table.

subfigures.description: Phonon dispersion of FeAl: axes Energy (THz) vs high-symmetry path Γ–M–R–Γ–X, y ticks 0–10. A lower band group (max just below 8 THz near M) is separated by an optical gap from an upper group at ~10–11 THz that is nearly flat at ~10 THz at Γ.
Phonon dispersion of Fe3Al: Energy (THz) vs Γ–X–M–R–Γ, y ticks 0–10. Bands form a continuous dense manifold from 0 to above 10 THz with no optical gap and no negative-frequency (imaginary) branches.

Phonon dispersion of Fe3AlC: Energy (THz) plotted to 25 THz (ticks 0,5,10,15,20,25). A sparse group of branches between ~20 and ~26 THz (one flat branch at 20 THz from Γ to X) is well separated from a dense lower manifold below ~15 THz. x-axis high-symmetry labels only partially legible.

panel (c): the exact number of individual high-frequency branches between 20 and 26 THz cannot be unambiguously counted due to curve overlap
